name: sanctuary-r1
note: The Oracle's Sanctuary (owner, 2026-10-23, option 1: the Oracle grounded in The Winter's Tale's oracle of Delphos): the Shiro row becomes her sanctuary, the scroll shop, a monolithic stone sister site to the Ancient Temple. Two concepts, two candidates each.

sanctuary-cleft.prompt: CAMERA AND STYLE REFERENCE: the first attached panel on grass is a building from this game drawn in the game's camera and in this style; match its camera exactly (the front square to the viewer, no side view, the top seen from above, the grid straight), its painterly rendering and its bright daylight. SIBLING REFERENCE: the second attached panel is this game's ANCIENT TEMPLE, a mossy ruin of the same lost civilisation; the sanctuary shares its pale weathered stone, its moss, and the carved glyphs on its stones, but is a DIFFERENT kind of place: not a ruin, not a building, an open sanctuary in use. SUBJECT: the ORACLE'S SANCTUARY at Delphos, where Apollo's sealed scrolls are bought (the Ancient Temple opens them). It must read at a glance as a sacred, oracular stone place: monolithic, ancient, alive. Palette: pale sun-warmed limestone, bronze, laurel green, moss, a little gold. LOOK: valley: grown into nature, moss on the stone, wildflowers, no vines over the glyphs. No people. CONCEPT A, THE CLEFT: a shelf of pale living rock with a dark narrow CLEFT split through its middle, a faint warm golden glow deep inside the cleft (light only, no vapour); over the cleft stands a tall bronze TRIPOD with a shallow bowl; around it four or five tall MONOLITHIC standing stones of pale limestone, rough-hewn, carved with the same glyphs as the Temple, leaning a little, the tallest rising high; a flat altar stone at the front with three sealed scrolls, a laurel wreath and a small bronze bowl on it; two laurel trees, one each side; stone steps up onto the shelf; moss in the cracks. The LAST attached image is a layout guide, a patch of the board grid with a tan 4 x 4 square: the sanctuary's stones, terrace and props fill that 4 x 4 square almost to its edges, end to end (the tallest pillars and the laurel may rise above it), with soft contact shadows. Fill the surrounding squares with plain short grass in the same style, no props beyond those named, and draw the faint grid lines as thin tile edges. Do not leave the tan square tan. No letters anywhere, no people, no smoke, no steam, no vapour.

Its stone is TOO DARK AND TOO GREY: the owner is missing the Temple's white light. Redraw the sanctuary identical in every way (every stone, the tripod, the cleft and its glow, the altar, scrolls, trees, steps, camera, composition, size) with ONE change only: paint every stone surface in EXACTLY the Temple's stone: the same near-white sunlit limestone, the same high-key lighting with bright faces and only light warm-grey shadows, the same chalky bloom, the same soft yellow-green moss sitting on white stone; no mid-grey, no beige, no dark shading. Side by side the two must look cut from the same block and lit by the same sun. The glyphs, bronze and laurels stay as they are. sanctuary-e.prompt: REFERENCE: the first attached panel is this game's ORACLE'S SANCTUARY as drawn; the owner approves its stone colour (white sunlit limestone) and everything in it. SHADOW REFERENCE: the second attached panel is this game's ANCIENT TEMPLE. Look at its SHADOWS: they are much STRONGER than the sanctuary's: deep, clearly darker shading on every face turned away from the light (the right and under sides of every stone), firm dark shadow in every recess, under every ledge and step, and a definite cast shadow on the ground to the lower right of each pillar and of the whole mass, so the stone has real weight and roundness. The sanctuary today is flat and washed out by comparison. Redraw the sanctuary identical in every way (every stone, the tripod, the cleft and its glow, the altar, scrolls, trees, steps, camera, composition, size, the same white stone colour) with ONE change only: the SHADOWS are as strong as the Temple's: the same light from high up and a little left, the same deep shading on the shadow sides of the standing stones and the shelf, dark recesses between the stones and under the steps and altar, and cast shadows on the shelf and the grass to the lower right; the sunlit faces stay bright white. The result must sit beside the Temple as one set, lit by the same sun.
